newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes mixed amid Pakistan tender.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes mixed amid Pakistan tender.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed mixed with export activity underpinning the market including news Pakistan soon would be in the market for 350,000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat, traders said.
A Pakistan embassy official said Pakistan will seek later this month roughly 350,000 tonnes of optional origin soft white wheat for Sept 11-Oct 10 delivery.

The wheat market moved higher around midday as traders opined the wheat market was due for a correction after declines this week that were triggered by a larger-than-expected wheat crop forecast for the U.S. by USDA.
Griffin Trading bought two million bushels of July, FIMAT Futures bought two million December and Smith Barney bought 1.5 million bushels of December, traders said.
Traders said some pressure was on the market from showers in portions of Australia and Argentina's wheat growing region.
Wheat closed 1-1/4 cents lower to three cents higher, with September down 1-1/4 at $3.54 per bushel and December down the same at $3.69-1/2.

In spread dealings, Prudential Securities did 1.5 million bushels of September/December at 15-1/2 cents, premium December and Tenco Inc did one million September/December at 15-1/2 cents, premium December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 17,000 contracts, below the 18,291 traded Thursday.
In wheat options, Tenco Inc bought 350 December $3.70 calls at 19 cents, Smith Barney bought 250 December $4.10 puts at 45-1/2 cents and sold 250 December $3.90 puts at 30 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,000 contracts, above the 2,855 traded Thursday.
